Plot a gg_boost_prediction object

Source: R/plot.gg_boost_prediction.R
autoplot.gg_boost_prediction.Rd

Each subject's predicted response at a fixed time, against one covariate.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gg_boost_prediction'
autoplot(object, covariate, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gg_boost_prediction'
plot(x, covariate, ...)

Arguments

object

A gg_boost_prediction object.

covariate

Name of the covariate to place on the x axis.

...

Passed to geom_point.

x

A gg_boost_prediction object.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

For a numeric covariate every subject is a point and a loess smoother traces the trend. The smoother summarises the points; it is not a partial effect, because the other covariates are left at each subject's own values. A flat smoother over a wide scatter says the covariate matters little at this time and the others drive the spread.

For a factor covariate the points are grouped by level with each level's mean marked.

The returned plot carries no theme.

See also

gg_boost_prediction

Examples

# \donttest{
sim <- boostmtree::simLong(n = 25, n.time = 4, model = 1)$data.list
fit <- boostmtree::boostmtree(
  x = sim$features, tm = sim$time, id = sim$id, y = sim$y,
  M = 50, cv.flag = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
plot(gg_boost_prediction(fit, time = 1), covariate = "x1")

# }
